hints: First check whether the query lies on any edge.
Otherwise cast a horizontal ray and count boundary crossings.
Use a half-open vertical interval for each edge so a vertex is not counted twice.
analogy: A ray starting outside alternates between outside and inside whenever it crosses the polygon boundary.
example: For the square from (0,0) to (2,2), (1,1) is inside, (3,1) outside, and (0,1) on the boundary.
algorithm: For each query, test every edge for zero cross product and coordinate bounds; if found, report BOUNDARY. Otherwise count edges whose endpoints lie on opposite sides of the query's horizontal line and whose intersection is to the right, comparing with integer cross products. Report INSIDE for an odd count, OUTSIDE for an even count. Use wide arithmetic.
correctness: The boundary test detects all points on an edge. For every other point, each ray crossing toggles inside status; the half-open endpoint rule counts shared vertices consistently, so parity gives the correct status.
complexity: For n polygon vertices and m queries, O(nm) time and O(n) space.
